question_text: The 'X run' or simply 'X', is an iconic endurance run to X from Y. Until around 2014, when it was made optional in view of increased traffic along the X-Y route, this activity was a mainstay of life in Y and a rite of passage. Individuals assigned the run typically assembled at Y at 7am on Saturdays, attired in appropriate 'Field Service Marching Order Scale B' tactical gear, and were expected to reach the ~2000 ft X summit by 9am. The rigorous hike serves as a useful training exercise to test and develop stamina and mental fortitude, while also simulating real-world operations in challenging and rugged terrain. It is also not uncommon for visiting delegations from friendly and allied nations to participate, such as when a 300-member team from Australia hiked up X in 2024. X, which forms a backdrop of sorts to Y, imbues both the stated mission of Y and the 'X run' with deep historical significance. Give X, Y.
answer_text: X - Sinhagad Fort. Y - National Defence Academy.

question_text: The 2025 film 'Hero in the Making' is intended as a celebration of the life and career of X. The synopsis notes his fearless nature and temperament, and that 'X's journey is one of pure passion and persistence.' X's dominant personality is amply illustrated by the movie cover art, which depicts X majestically perched on a Game of Thrones-style Iron Throne. Give X.
answer_text: X - Sahibzada Farhan (Pakistani cricketer; the film is a satirical reference to his celebratory batting style).

question_text: Below is an excerpt from a New York Times article on a certain topic: "The arguments from both sides are old, repetitive and made from frozen positions. What is new is the gravity of the fighting and its tendency to escalate. There are no such things any longer as strictly local wars. If this one grows and moves past a point of no return, the whole of Asia could be shaken in even worse fashion than it now is... __________ expressed alarm at his latest news conference, but the only hope he could offer was that 'the U.N. is already involved, and we hope that the constructive efforts of the Secretary General may be successful there.' However, the United Nations has been trying in vain for eighteen years to settle the _________ dispute. Mr. ____'s latest attempt to send X to _____ and _______ was met by conditions from both countries which completely discouraged him. Yet both are committed by an accord to arbitrate their border disputes." A stalwart diplomat, sociologist and negotiator, X gained renown for his contributions in peacefully resolving several high-profile conflicts worldwide. His work greatly shaped how the United Nations approached and mediated in violent conflicts. Notably, he was the first ever person of African descent to win the Nobel Prize for his work in resolving another seemingly intractable conflict. ID the specific conflict referenced in this excerpt, and ID X (3+7 points).

Founded in 1982, this Florida-based company quickly became a world-leading maker of X systems and pioneered several innovative product ideas, including the home X system in the late 1980s. Its solid performance culminated in a 1994 listing on NASDAQ under the ticker $RIME. However, the company largely stagnated over the years due to increasing competition and rapid technological change, which rendered most of their product line obsolete. In 2024, X rebranded to 'Algorhythm Holdings, Inc.' It sold its X business to the Sting Ray group in late 2025 and reinvented itself as an AI-enabled freight and logistics platform. On February 12, 2026, it launched its platform SemiCar, which it claimed was already helping customers scale freight and cargo volumes by up to 400% with zero human intervention, according to a report in The Guardian. This one claim in a company whitepaper triggered a global frenzy, and $RIME has zoomed over 200% since. Stocks across the shipping and logistics sectors took a huge beating, with some US-based trucking companies shedding 15% of their market cap in a single day. Giants like DHL, UPS, and Maersk also saw steep share price drops, as investors adopted what analysts call a 'sell first, ask questions later if the word AI appears in the headline' approach. Chronicling this madness, a LinkedIn post titled 'From X to Kill Mode' noted: 'We are officially in an era where the fear of AI disruption is so high that even the most established industries aren't safe from the X effect. Maersk is still a behemoth, but for one day in February 2026, the world decided that a X pivot was more powerful than a fleet of 700 container ships. Moral of the story: If you want your stock price to double, just stop selling _________ and start selling "Logistics Intelligence."' Give X or the product.
answer_text: X - The Singing Machine Company (Karaoke Machines).

question_text: On the left is a poem by Richard Brautigan. Written in 1967, it expresses a utopian vision of harmony and synchronicity between humans and technology. Some critics challenge the conventional interpretation however, suggesting that the poem is in fact an ironic satire of a future dystopia in which humans have subordinated ourselves to advanced technology. On the right is pictured an industrial rock band of the same name, which was inspired by this poem. For all this preamble, this somewhat obscure sci-fi themed poem entered popular discourse in October 2024 thanks to a seminal essay by X, a wide-ranging exploration of very similar ideas in keeping with our time of rapid technological upheaval. Give X.
answer_text: X - Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic. The essay is 'Machines of Loving Grace' (same title as the Brautigan poem and the band).

question_text: Looking back on a certain deal a few years after the fact, X claimed to regret acquiescing to many of Y's demands, chalking up the lack of resistance to desperation and financial precarity. In particular, a major modification was made at Y's behest to make the work in question sound less archaic and more appealing to a wider audience. This was in addition to myriad edits to fit the cultural context in which Y operated. Examples included renaming food items and altering certain terms of endearment. Scholars such as Philip Nel have criticized some of these translations as fundamentally changing the meaning and severing the connection to relevant concepts. However, Nel has also acknowledged Y's edits as resulting in an overall more sensitive text. ID X, Y and the specific, major change that was made during adaptation (3+4+3).
answer_text: X - J.K. Rowling. Y - Scholastic, Inc. The change: the US edition of 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' was renamed 'Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone' (along with renaming food items and terms of endearment for a US audience).

question_text: In Southeast Asia, London's the craze, Lest Malay sets us lost in a maze. While in London itself, Indigo's in sight, Swapping out places for colors delight. The Pakistanis cherish their fine Indigo cue, But give a friendly nod to Italy too. In Atlanta, you'll rarely mix up your fix, For there, they'll always honor proud Dixie tricks. Some regions, they stay spry upright, Eschewing the bottle to keep their path right. Yet some toast George Washington, glasses held high, While others just stick to their White in the sky! What am I referring to with this horribly written (and probably nonsensical) poem? General funda ok (need specific keywords).
answer_text: Local variants and modifications to the NATO Phonetic Alphabet: in SE Asia, Lima is often replaced by London (Lima = Malay word for five); in London, Indigo is used in lieu of India; in Pakistan, Indigo or Italy is used to avoid saying India; Atlanta airport uses Dixie or David in place of Delta (to avoid confusion with the airline); in some Islamic countries, White or Washington is used to avoid saying Whiskey.

question_text: In the context of the 2026 Economic Survey, we have discussed the poor performance of Indian school students on standardized mathematics tests despite increased enrollment and investments. These shoddy results spurred X and Y to undertake their own investigation of probable causes and remedies. X was particularly struck by the prodigious mental math abilities of children who worked in shops, admiring their ability to perform complex and involved calculations on the fly. He expected such experiences to confer advantages in classroom learning. However, in a comprehensive study involving children from Delhi and Kolkata, X and Y discovered that while the 'market kids' did extremely well on problems with concrete real-world significance, they struggled on far easier problems in tests. In contrast, school students who had no work experience did reasonably well on rule-based arithmetic questions but were completely ineffectual in applying their skills to practical problems. These findings suggest a lack of transferability in either direction and underline the need for more culturally relevant teaching methods. Explaining these findings, Y noted that 'The market kids are able to exploit base 10, so they do better on base 10 problems. The school kids have no idea. It makes no difference to them. The market kids may have additional tricks of this sort that we did not see.' With all this information, ID X and Y, whom we know for a related if slightly different reason.
answer_text: X - Abhijit Banerjee. Y - Esther Duflo. (Nobel laureates in Economics, known for 'Children's arithmetic skills do not transfer between applied and academic mathematics', Nature 2025.)

question_text: 'Ana Ng' is a 1989 song by the alternative rock band They Might Be Giants. The title was inspired by the large number of Ng (a common Vietnamese last name) listings in New York City telephone directories. It was to become their most successful, reaching No. 11 on the US Billboard Modern Rock Chart. The song is essentially about unrequited love, and critics such as Robert Christgau have praised the song as a 'beyond-perfect tour de force about a Vietnamese woman they never got to meet.' Discussing the second key theme in the song, bandmember John Linnell claimed that it was inspired by an old Pogo comic strip which depicts characters digging a hole with a certain objective, when one of them simply shoots a desktop _______ and checks where the exit wound appears. According to members and fans, the song is thus set somewhere near Peru. What is special about the titular Ana Ng? Give funda.
answer_text: Antipodal lover. The song lyrics talk about blowing a hole through the world to reach her. Vietnam and Peru are near-antipodal to each other.
